needs.title: Report transport and malformed-response failures as incomplete collection results
needs.what_is_missing_or_wrong: Network exceptions from the transport and invalid JSON bodies currently escape `collect()` instead of producing the module’s advertised honest, incomplete result. This can terminate a collection without preserving already collected candidates or a usable reason.
needs.what_done_would_look_like: Catch transport/decoding failures at the collection boundary, return `CollectResult(complete=False)` with retained candidates, pages fetched, search parameters, and a clear failure reason; add fake-transport and malformed-body tests.
tree_evidence: gitseed/collect/search.py:171 calls `transport.get()` without exception handling.
gitseed/collect/search.py:123 calls `json.loads()` without handling decode errors.
gitseed/collect/search.py:146-150 promises to stop loudly and report what happened.
tests/test_collect.py:186-189 covers HTTP 500, while tests/test_collect.py:354-357 covers malformed items but not malformed JSON or transport failures.
needs.distinct_from_others_because: This concerns resilience to unavailable or invalid responses, rather than rate-limit retry classification or grading-model validation.

needs.title: Classify the response after a rate-limit retry correctly
needs.what_is_missing_or_wrong: After waiting and retrying, every non-2xx response is reported as “still rate limited,” even if the retry is a permissions failure or a different HTTP error. That gives the caller a false diagnosis and can conceal an actionable authorization problem.
needs.what_done_would_look_like: Branch on the retry response classification just as the initial response does: retain the rate-limit message only for another limit response, report forbidden as permissions-related, and report other status failures accurately. Add tests for a rate-limit response followed by 403-with-budget and by 5xx.
tree_evidence: gitseed/collect/search.py:192-194 reclassifies the retry only to test for `ok`, then labels every failure “still rate limited.”
gitseed/collect/search.py:196-200 already distinguishes forbidden from generic errors for initial responses.
tests/test_collect.py:178-218 verifies initial permissions failures; tests/test_collect.py:234-245 verifies a second rate-limit response, but no test covers a changed retry failure type.
needs.distinct_from_others_because: This is specifically about preserving the correct cause across a retry, not handling exceptions or smoke-test behavior.

needs.title: Fail smoke validation when the grading backend changes model during sampled runs
needs.what_is_missing_or_wrong: The smoke gate records the first sampled model but only checks score drift. A client that silently serves different models across repeated identical evaluations can pass and be reported as trusted under the first model name, undermining reproducibility and provenance.
needs.what_done_would_look_like: Compare `GradeResult.model` across all repeated evaluations (and fail with an explanatory message when it changes); add a fake client whose model changes between calls and assert the smoke result fails.
tree_evidence: gitseed/grade/smoke.py:135-136 takes the displayed model solely from `repeats[0]`.
gitseed/grade/smoke.py:117-125 defines determinism only in terms of `idea` and `skill`.
gitseed/grade/smoke.py:121-124 states that reproducible rankings are the rationale for the determinism gate.
tests/test_smoke.py:19-59 provides score-drifting behavior, and tests/test_smoke.py:94-97 tests it, but none vary the returned model identifier.
needs.distinct_from_others_because: This is a grading provenance and reproducibility gap, independent of collection HTTP failure handling.

ranking.why_not_the_scout_order: The scout's own ordering could reflect what it found easiest to describe, and a quality score would let an operator prefer the need that looks likely to build. A hash of the need's own content is fixed before anyone knows which one survives.
